title: GS21 with the priced y factor on production, exposure = standardized PRODUCTIVITY x standardized COUPON (gs_bv 0.2; a product of two firm states, no type)
question: Does a priced second factor make a fair gap in GS21 when the exposure is the PRODUCT of two within-firm states that two different characteristics reveal, so the premium is bilinear in the ranks?
notes:
WHY (2026-10-10, 23:50). Seven y-factor constructions left GS21's premium 82-89% linear in the ranks of its characteristics, because in every one the exposure entered as a LEVEL (a type, a cost share, an option share, leverage), and a level that one characteristic reveals is spanned by a linear fit. The reduced-form exercise of the same night (rf_model nlat / nf_lat: factors loaded by PRODUCTS of partly observed latent firm states) and KP14's and BGN's measured footprints say room comes from a premium that is a product of two firm variables revealed by different characteristics. This spec does that in GS21's own states, with NO firm type: the y exposure is gs_bv * z~ * b~, standardized idiosyncratic productivity times standardized coupon (b~ = (b - 0.5)/0.29 on the unit grid), so the premium is bilinear in what roe and leverage reveal, has no additive part, and has a near-zero cross-sectional mean. Single solve.

PRE-CHECK (low resolution, xnum 41, znum 50, bnum 10, NY 9, 300 firms, scratchpad gsshape.py): at gs_bv 0.2 a linear fit on ranks of (roe, lev, size, bm) explains 34% of the true premium and pairwise products 80% (gvy25: 82% and 88%); the EW market reaches 40% of SR_max (gvy25 84%); cs-sd of the premium 7.4 %/yr; the mean premium is NEGATIVE (-2.6 %/yr: the typical firm is a hedge at this exposure) and the firm is about seven times larger than at gs_bv 0 (the convexity of e^{exposure y} in the exposure raises value). gs_bv 0.4 and 0.8 make the value explode. gs_bv 0.1 and 0.15 are being probed as safer points.

CHECKS. E[M R] = 1 to 1e-15 at low resolution; gs_bzb = 0 reproduces the solver exactly.

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; id read from the Quest solve log by verify_gs_vy_klc.sh before any seed runs. This is a mechanism probe, not a calibrated GS21.

PREDICTION (2026-10-10, before the run). Market share of SR_max below 50%; room above +0.03 with room_s close to room (the bilinear term is static in the ranks given the state); fair gap +0.005 to +0.015. FALSIFIED as 'a product exposure makes the KP mechanism work in GS21' if room_s is below +0.02 at the oracle stage or the fair gap is below +0.005.

changes: gs_bv 0.2 x gs_bzb 1.0 z~ b~: productivity x coupon exposure, single type; gs_bzl 0, gs_bzi 0, bv_comp 0
the y factor moves the COST, exp(gs_bc y), with types gs_bc [0.0]; production exposure gs_bv 0, no level compensation (at y = 0 every type pays the same cost)
everything else gvy25's: 9-node priced y chain, gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35

method.gs_vy_exposure: production x exp(gs_bv gs_bzb z~ b~ y)

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks and the aggregate y path (reg_seed offset by the seed).
